lead.headline: Coldcard RNG Failure Exposes $130M Self-Custody Risk as Mastercard Bets $1.8B on Stablecoin Infrastructure
lead.tldr: The largest hardware wallet exploit in history reveals that self-custody security assumptions were underpriced by the market, while institutional capital continues to flow toward stablecoin rails and away from Bitcoin base-layer exposure.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, this week a single firmware bug in a device marketed as 'hyper-secure' rewrote how we underwrite custody risk in Bitcoin.

top_signals.title: Your Keys, Not Your Coins: Coldcard Wallets Hacked for $130m and Counting
top_signals.summary: Coldcard hardware wallets have reportedly been compromised, resulting in losses of $130 million and counting. The incident highlights that removing third-party custodians transfers custody risk to the hardware and key-generation processes.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The $130M Coldcard compromise demonstrates that removing custodians does not remove custody risk—it relocates it to hardware supply chains and firmware verification processes that most investors have not modeled.

top_signals.title: Inside the COLDCARD Entropy Failure w/ Alex Thorn
top_signals.summary: A critical RNG firmware bug in CoinKite Coldcard hardware wallets has led to an exploit compromising over 1,500 BTC (valued at $100M+). The attack utilized open-source AI models to operationalize the drainer bots, raising concerns about the security of Bitcoin self-custody.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The use of open-source AI models to operationalize drainer bots introduces a scalable attack vector that lowers the technical barrier for exploiting entropy failures, making this not a one-off but a template.

top_signals.title: Coldcard Bitcoin theft tops $100M across 3 confirmed attack waves: Galaxy
top_signals.summary: A critical vulnerability in Coldcard hardware wallets has led to Bitcoin thefts exceeding $100 million across three confirmed attack waves. Galaxy has warned that these attacks are ongoing, and investigators are collaborating with US authorities to track attacker addresses.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Galaxy's confirmation of three ongoing attack waves with US law enforcement involvement signals that the exploit surface is still expanding and that attribution efforts may create regulatory precedents for hardware wallet liability.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin owners rocked by $116 million hack: What we know about the Coldcard exploit
top_signals.summary: A massive security breach has targeted Coldcard cold storage wallets, resulting in the theft of 1,816 Bitcoin. The exploit is particularly concerning as it compromised wallets previously considered hyper-secure.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The 1,816 BTC theft from wallets previously considered 'hyper-secure' will force repricing of self-custody premiums and likely accelerate institutional preference for insured custody or regulated stablecoin holdings.

top_signals.title: Landmark crypto bill stalls in US Senate despite $225mn spending push
top_signals.summary: A major cryptocurrency bill has stalled in the US Senate despite a significant $225 million lobbying effort. Lawmakers remain divided over the legislation, hindering the passage of a top priority for the crypto industry.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The $225M lobbying failure reveals that even unprecedented industry spending cannot overcome partisan gridlock, pushing regulatory certainty further into 2027 and raising the cost of capital for US-facing protocols.

top_signals.title: Coldcard exploit pushes July losses to $247M as second-worst month of 202614m
top_signals.summary: A security exploit affecting Coldcard has contributed to July becoming the second-worst month for losses in 2026. Total losses for the month have reached $247 million.
top_signals.why_it_matters: July's $247M total makes it the second-worst month of 2026, with Coldcard representing the majority of losses, confirming that security incidents rather than macro conditions are now the dominant downside driver in crypto.

deals.summary: Mastercard has finalized the acquisition of BVNK for $1.8 billion to strengthen its stablecoin capabilities. The move aims to provide banks and fintechs with enhanced tools for stablecoin payments, settlements, and treasury services.

Japanese stablecoin issuer JPYC has raised $38 million in an extended Series B funding round. The company intends to use the capital to expand its Web3 ecosystem and drive the adoption of its stablecoin.

DePIN project Vangrid has raised $9 million in a token round to develop a spatial data network designed for physical AI. The project currently utilizes a bounty system for contributors and plans to launch its native token later this year.

Bitmine has increased its Ethereum holdings by $19.6 million and repurchased 4.5 million of its own shares. The company is actively working toward a target of owning 5% of the total circulating supply of Ether.
Fintech startup Moss has achieved unicorn status with a valuation of €1bn. The company secured this milestone following a €30m Series C funding round for its AI finance platform.

Fortitude Mining, a subsidiary of DCG, has acquired a 12.5 MW mining facility in Nebraska. The acquisition was completed for a net cost of approximately $4.7 million and is intended to expand the company's Zcash mining operations.

on_the_radar.title: Putin signs landmark crypto law allowing regulated retail trading in Russia
on_the_radar.summary: President Vladimir Putin has signed a landmark law that legalizes regulated retail trading of cryptocurrencies in Russia. While domestic payments for goods and services remain banned, the law explicitly permits the use of digital assets for cross-border settlements.

on_the_radar.title: Western Union brings stablecoin remittances to Visa network with Stablecard27m
on_the_radar.summary: Western Union is integrating stablecoin-based remittances into the Visa network via Stablecard. This move aims to modernize cross-border payments by leveraging blockchain technology for faster and more efficient transfers.

on_the_radar.title: BlackRock brings tokenized money market funds to Europe via JPMorgan28m, BlackRock brings tokenized money market funds to Europe via JPMorganJPMorgan’s Kinexys platform will tokenize select BlackRock money market fund shares denominated in pounds, euros and US dollars.
on_the_radar.summary: BlackRock is expanding its tokenization efforts in Europe by utilizing JPMorgan's Kinexys platform to tokenize money market fund shares. These assets will be denominated in US dollars, euros, and British pounds, marking a significant step in institutional RWA adoption.

on_the_radar.title: BitGo moves $7.4 billion Wrapped Bitcoins to Chainlink CCIP in latest LayerZero exodus
on_the_radar.summary: BitGo has migrated $7.4 billion in Wrapped Bitcoins (WBTC) from LayerZero to Chainlink's Cross-Chain Interoperability Protocol (CCIP). This move contributes to a larger trend where nearly $15 billion in assets have shifted away from LayerZero toward Chainlink.

on_the_radar.title: BlackRock launches two tokenized money market funds for stablecoin reserves
on_the_radar.summary: BlackRock has launched two tokenized money market funds specifically designed to hold stablecoin reserves. This move places the asset manager alongside other financial giants like Morgan Stanley and Fidelity in providing institutional-grade reserve solutions.

on_the_radar.title: BlackRock launches tokenized money market funds for stablecoin reserves37m
on_the_radar.summary: BlackRock has introduced tokenized money market funds specifically designed to serve as reserves for stablecoins. This move integrates traditional financial liquidity management with blockchain-based digital assets.

on_the_radar.title: World Liberty received $100 million from businessman investigated for money laundering: NYT
on_the_radar.summary: World Liberty Financial reportedly received $100 million from businessman Guren 'Bobby' Zhou. Zhou is currently under investigation by British officials for money laundering, although no charges have been filed.

on_the_radar.title: BTCPay restricts remote Lightning access after attackers steal funds34m, BTCPay restricts remote Lightning access after attackers steal fundsFoundation and Citadel21 reported drained Lightning nodes, but the total amount stolen and number of affected operators remain unknown.
on_the_radar.summary: BTCPay has restricted remote access to Lightning nodes following a series of attacks that resulted in stolen funds. The Foundation and Citadel21 reported drained nodes, though the total financial impact is currently unknown.

on_the_radar.title: US spot Bitcoin ETFs post best week since April with $1B inflows39m, US spot Bitcoin ETFs post best week since April with $1B inflowsThe spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds registered their third-strongest showing since October as institutional demand showed signs of renewed momentum.
on_the_radar.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs experienced their strongest weekly performance since April, recording $1 billion in inflows. This surge indicates a renewal of institutional demand for Bitcoin through regulated investment vehicles.

on_the_radar.title: US Senate to vote on advancing CLARITY Act on Sept. 15 after Thune files cloture
on_the_radar.summary: The US Senate is scheduled to vote on advancing the CLARITY Act on September 15 following a cloture filing by Senator Thune. The act aims to establish clearer market-structure rules and ethics provisions for the cryptocurrency industry.

on_the_radar.title: Bitcoin, ether ETFs draw $1.1 billion in best inflow week since April, despite low volume
on_the_radar.summary: Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs experienced their strongest inflow week since April, totaling $1.1 billion. Analyst Eric Balchunas suggests this trend may be linked to reactions following a Coldcard wallet exploit.

on_the_radar.title: BTCPay warns of actively exploited vulnerability that could drain funds
on_the_radar.summary: BTCPay has issued an urgent warning regarding an actively exploited vulnerability that could lead to the draining of user funds. Users are strongly advised to update their servers to version 2.4.2 immediately to secure their assets.

linkedin_post:
We have underwritten self-custody hardware as a risk reduction. The Coldcard exploit—1,816 BTC gone through a firmware RNG bug now weaponized with open-source AI—suggests we mispriced it. The device was marketed as hyper-secure. The market believed it. Galaxy counts three attack waves and counting, with US authorities now tracing addresses. This is not a user error story. It is a supply chain and entropy verification failure that scales.

The question for our portfolio: where does capital rotate when self-custody premiums get repriced? One place is already visible. Mastercard paid $1.8 billion for BVNK this week, adding stablecoin settlement rails for banks and fintechs. JPYC raised $38 million in Tokyo. The infrastructure bet is on regulated, intermediated stablecoin flows—not on hardening Bitcoin base-layer custody for retail.

We are watching whether Ethereum and Solana inflation schedule debates, flagged by Galaxy and Messari this week, become the next repricing catalyst. If issuance burns taper without killing validator economics, the token models shift. If they fail, the yield compression thesis for L1s takes another hit.

Our test: does Q3 see a hardware wallet insurance market emerge, or does capital simply flee to stablecoin wrappers? We are underwriting the latter.
